title: The Battle Before The Battle
subtitle: When The Leader Needs To Be Liked
tagline: The need to be loved by everyone can eventually make a leader unable to faithfully lead anyone.
headline: When Leaders Need to Be Liked
headline_sub: Are You Leading People or Managing Their Opinion of You?
seo_title: When Leaders Need to Be Liked | TheWrkShop
seo_description: The need to be loved by everyone can make a leader unable to lead anyone. A biblical look at people-pleasing for leaders at work, on teams and at home.

hero_image_alt: A crowned king looks down on a cheering crowd while a leader sits head bowed at a boardroom table as people press in on him: When the Leader Needs to Be Liked.

scriptures.text: Then Saul said to Samuel, “I have sinned. I violated the LORD’s command and your instructions. I was afraid of the men and so I gave in to them.”
If I were still trying to please people, I would not be a servant of Christ.

blocks.text: Saul finally says it.
“I was afraid of the men….”
Then:
“….I gave in to them.”
That’s leadership failure before the leadership failure.
Saul had authority over the people.
But internally:
THE PEOPLE HAD AUTHORITY OVER SAUL.

items: But approval was governing him internally.

blocks.text: That’s dangerous.
Because when a leader needs the room to like him, the room can begin leading the leader.
“IF THEY’RE HAPPY WITH ME, I MUST BE LEADING WELL.”
Not necessarily.
Because leaders occasionally have to:
If approval becomes your compass:
YOU WILL EVENTUALLY CONFUSE DISAPPOINTING PEOPLE WITH FAILING PEOPLE.
Those aren’t the same thing.
Exodus 32.

items: They want gods they can see.

blocks.text: And instead of forming the people toward faithfulness:
THE PEOPLE’S DESIRE BEGINS FORMING THE LEADER.
The golden calf is not merely a story about rebellious followers.
It is also a warning about leadership that gives anxious people what they demand instead of helping them remain faithful while they wait.
Sometimes leadership means refusing to baptize the crowd’s impatience.
LOVE PEOPLE WITHOUT NEEDING THEIR APPROVAL TO OBEY GOD.
“I don’t care what anybody thinks” can become pride too.
But ultimately:
APPROVAL CANNOT BECOME LORD.
Paul says:
“If I were still trying to please people, I would not be a servant of Christ.”
There is an allegiance issue underneath leadership.

items: WHO AM I MOST AFRAID TO DISAPPOINT?
HAVE I AVOIDED A NECESSARY CONVERSATION BECAUSE I WANTED TO REMAIN LIKED?
HAVE I SAID YES WHEN FAITHFULNESS REQUIRED NO?
AM I LEADING PEOPLE OR MANAGING THEIR OPINION OF ME?

blocks.text: Then:
IF NOBODY APPLAUDED THIS DECISION, WOULD I STILL BELIEVE IT WAS FAITHFUL?
Before making the next difficult leadership decision, pray:
“Father, remove my need to control how everyone feels about me.”
Then ask:
WHAT DOES FAITHFULNESS REQUIRE?
When a leader needs the room to like him, the room can begin leading the leader.
Father,
Free me from needing approval to feel secure.
Keep me tender toward people without becoming controlled by their reactions.

items: Give me courage to disappoint when faithfulness requires it.
Wisdom to listen when correction is needed.
And humility to know the difference.
Jesus is Lord of my leadership.

blocks.text: Saul had authority over the people, but the people had authority over Saul.
You can hold the title and still be led by the room.
Don’t confuse disappointing people with failing people.
Love people without needing their approval to obey God.
Am I leading people, or managing their opinion of me?
-TheWrkShop
